title: Holmes OSF · Experiment 4 · Driving and pedal response
citation: Holmes, N. P., Martin, D. J., Mitchell, W., Noorani, Z., & Thorne, A. (2020). Do sounds near the hand facilitate tactile reaction times? Four experiments and a meta-analysis provide mixed support and suggest a small effect size. OSF 73x59, manuscript revision 4.
notes: Inspect the author project's simulator task. The Designer shows the 2.875 ms far cue lead rounded to the nearest millisecond.

published_method.source_version: March 2020 manuscript revision 4 in the 2019 OSF project, alongside ExperimentX task code and archived digital command records.

driving_conditions.Away: Watch replay with hands beside the wheel. Stimulate right index finger.
driving_conditions.Passive: Hold the wheel and watch a replay. Stimulate the wheel at the right hand.
driving_conditions.Active: Operate the simulator with the same wheel stimulation site.

published_method.trial_schedule: Three counterbalanced driving conditions, with 30 trials per near/far distance within each condition, for 180 trials.
published_method.response: Brake as quickly as possible after feeling vibration. The 150 ms detection start is measured from the tactile command.

stimulus_type.value: Car horn waveform for auditory distractor and vibrotactile drive.

source_provenance.value: Author's OSF Experiment4 folder supplies the exact car horn MP3 input and driving.m.
source_provenance.source: OSF Experiment4 driving.m, settings and trial loop

stimulus_duration.source: Manuscript pp. 18–20, Experiment 4; OSF Experiment4 driving.m, settings and trial loop
stimulus_duration.gap: Published value rounds the 3500-sample segment at 8000 output samples/s.

gain_envelope.source: OSF Experiment4 driving.m, settings and trial loop
gain_envelope.gap: Code multipliers. Physical SPL calibration unreported.

renderer_or_apparatus.value: Driving Simulator 2013, computer steering wheel and foot pedals. Vibrator on right index or right rear of wheel. Two fixed speakers.

value: Car horn vibration with near sound
Car horn vibration with far sound

condition_intermixing.value: Pseudorandom near/far trials within each of the three driving-related conditions.

blocked_or_random_order.value: One 60-trial block per condition. Away, Passive and Active order counterbalanced.

iti_jitter_policy.source: Manuscript pp. 18–20, Experiment 4; OSF Experiment4 driving.m, settings and trial loop
iti_jitter_policy.gap: Public code draws uniform pretrial delay. ITI variable is defined but unused in that trial loop. Between-block breaks varied by cohort.

response_window.source: OSF Experiment4 driving.m, settings and trial loop
response_window.gap: Code locates pedal input in recorded samples. Separate timeout behavior beyond the window is unreported.

task_sequence_rules.value: Press brake pedal as soon as vibration is felt while watching or playing the simulator.

soa_table.source: Manuscript pp. 18–20, Experiment 4; OSF Experiment4 driving.m, settings and trial loop
soa_table.gap: Paper reports 2.5 and 70 cm speaker distances and no exact scheduling offset. Code computes 23 samples at 8 kHz from a different pair of distances (5 and 105 cm). Do not infer measured arrival synchrony.

baseline_strategy.gap: Each trial pairs horn vibration with sound.

catch_trial_type.gap: All 60 trials per block contain a tactile target.

catch_count.gap: No no-touch trials reported in the stated allocation.

implementation_gaps: Recreate the driving simulator with independent video replay and active steering sessions, acquire pedal timing and switch tactile loop from index to wheel by condition.
Recover or validate horn samples and calibration, audio/tactile coupling and near/far speaker routing. Exact delivered physical timing is unverified.
Reconcile manuscript and source-code timing, recover a repeatable order policy, and retain the corresponding apparatus setup for each condition.
reference_parameters.planner_scope: The study settings describe the source procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for this profile.
